lee: Heads up — we're seeing a p99 latency spike on /v1/generate after the deploy that landed at 2169989000. Canary shows 3x tail latency and compile-queue builds are enormous. Anyone started a bisect?
priya: starting bisect now. suspect candidates: #5428 (kernel selector rewrite), #5433 (batching heuristic tweak). kicking off bisection job.
sam: quick metrics dump from canary:
```
compile_queue.rate = 2400 ops/min (baseline 60)
evictions/sec = 180 (baseline 4)
compile_failures = 12/min
```
This looks like a compile storm + KV cache thrash.
ci-bot: perf/compile_queue benchmark failed on CI: 12.3% reg vs baseline — https://ci.redwood/teams/eng-runtime/runs/8349
maya: I reproduced locally with a seq=1024 workload, small batch. If I force seq=64 the issue disappears. Something changed selector behavior for short/medium sequences.
lee: added logging to kernel selector decisions on canary; sample output:
```
[2169992400] selector: input_len=58 -> policy=meta-sway-v2 -> picked=fast-fused-kernel-int8
[2169992401] selector: input_len=300 -> policy=meta-sway-v2 -> picked=large-kernel-fp16
[2169992402] selector: input_len=16 -> policy=meta-sway-v2 -> picked=large-kernel-fp16  <- wrong for small seq
```
That last line shows meta-sway-v2 prefers a heavier kernel for very short sequences (wrong pick), causing extra compiles and cache misses.
priya: can confirm — the new scoring in #5428 gives more weight to aggregated throughput, which biases toward kernels with high amortized perf, but it doesn't account for extra compile overhead when the KV cache is cold. So policy drift.
sam: quick mitigation: set REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=stable in canary env. did that, and compile_queue rate dropped to ~80 ops/min and p99 returned to baseline.
maya: hotfix verified on canary: p50/p95/p99 all within tolerance. Will open a PR to make the env flip reversible and gated by feature flag.
priya: propose revert of #5428 for now, and follow-up PR to rework scoring to include compile-cost penalty and kv-cache-residency heuristics. I'll draft revert PR and a postmortem.
ops-bot: canary rollout paused by ops due to SLA alert. Revert PR is queued.
lee: marking this thread as rollout-blocker. running full bisect to isolate exact commit in #5428 that introduced the weight change. assigning owners: @priya (bisect), @maya (local repro), @sam (ops mitigation).
sam: FYI I collected flamegraphs and traces: https://redwood-internal/snapshots/216999/fg.svg and heap/kv-stats: https://s3.redwood/perf/216999/kv_dump.json
priya: created revert PR #5461, CI green for revert branch. request review from @eng-runtime leads.
maya: after revert merges, canary looks stable. let's schedule a small gated rollout and make sure to include a perf test targeting small seq workloads.
lee: thanks everyone. we'll include a checkpoint in the postmortem: add compile-cost to selector scoring, add an integration perf test for seq=16/64/1024 combos, and improve KV cache metrics visibility.
sam: noted. :thumbsup:
priya: filing postmortem and retrospective actions now. :spiral_note_pad:
